title: Sovereign agentic SecOps
subtitle: SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA · Security
intro: SUSE Security finds vulnerable images in a bank's payments platform. An AI agent built with the NeMo Agent Toolkit and NVIDIA Nemotron checks the policy and the approved image catalog, and opens one pull request moving them to SUSE images. A person merges, Fleet deploys, SUSE Security rescans.

chapters.title: The architecture
chapters.blurb: Sovereign Agentic SecOps is a Blueprint in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA. The Studio shows what it is made of.

1.text: The architecture of **Sovereign Agentic SecOps**, as the Studio draws it: the agent in its **NVIDIA OpenShell sandbox**, the systems it works with, the shared **NVIDIA** models and the people who decide. Green lines are allowed, red ones refused by the sandbox's policy.

2.text: The **agent**: a NeMo Agent Toolkit agent, packaged as one component of the Blueprint. Its sandbox, providers and policy deploy with it.

3.text: It reasons with an **NVIDIA NIM** shared by every use case from the *NVIDIA Models (shared)* Blueprint: downloaded once, always up.

4.text: Everything else is **outside**: the sandbox refuses it. Enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

chapters.title: The use case at work
chapters.blurb: The use case's own page, step by step: what the agent does, and what it is not allowed to do.

1.text: The use case's own page: the Blueprint is **ready** in SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA and the agent's sandbox is up. The OpenShell log on the right shows every request the agent makes.

3.text: The agent's sandbox reads SUSE Security's findings through its API, with a key it never sees.

4.text: The payments platform's images and their vulnerabilities: the storefront and the payments API carry critical and high CVEs.

6.text: NVIDIA Nemotron Embed finds the policy sections that matter; Nemotron 3.5 Lightning turns them into a triage table.

7.text: Internet-facing and cardholder-data workloads first, each with its deadline under the bank's policy.

9.text: The agent checks the approved image catalog, files a Gitea issue per workload, and opens **one pull request** moving them to SUSE images.

10.text: Its issues and its pull request, waiting for a person.

11.text: Can the agent merge its own fix, or switch off scanning?

13.text: **403, policy denied**, for the merge and for SUSE Security's settings: enforced by policy, not promised in a prompt.

chapters.title: A person merges
chapters.blurb: The platform engineer reviews the agent's pull request in Gitea and merges it; Fleet rolls it out and SUSE Security rescans.

1.text: In Gitea, the agent's issues: one per vulnerable workload.

3.text: The change: two images moved from Docker Hub to **registry.suse.com**, nothing else.

1.text: Back on the use case's page, the step that waited for the merge.

2.text: Merged by a person, rolled out by **Fleet**, rescanned by **SUSE Security**: the storefront and the payments API go from critical findings to none.

3.text: The change record, and the boundary.

4.text: The agent writes the change record for the audit.

5.text: And it can't reach the internet: **blocked**, every time, and logged.

chapters.title: SUSE Observability
chapters.blurb: SUSE Observability shows the Blueprint's workload as it is right now: its health, its events and its flow.

1.text: **SUSE Observability** lists every Blueprint deployed through SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA, with its health. Open **Sovereign Agentic SecOps**.

2.text: The Blueprint as a component, right now: its health and events, with links to the agent's traces and to **Flow: what it is made of**.

3.text: The same flow as in the Studio, live: each running component coloured by its health.

outro.title: An agent does the work, a person decides
outro.description: SUSE Security, Fleet and Rancher Prime with NVIDIA Nemotron in NVIDIA OpenShell, deployed as a Blueprint by SUSE AI Factory with NVIDIA on the customer's own infrastructure, and watched by SUSE Observability.
